question: The proposed Catalan legislation on taxis and private hire vehicles (PHVs) would substantially restrict urban PHV services by introducing preferential treatment for taxis, market-access restrictions and minimum pre-booking periods. Notification of the bill was given under the EU procedure for notifying draft technical regulations (TRIS), offering an opportunity for Commission scrutiny.

However, the Commission’s detailed opinion addressed certain digital intermediation requirements, leaving the broader restrictions on PHVs unassessed. These restrictions appear incompatible with freedom of establishment under Article 49 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the Prestige and Limousine judgment (Case C-50/21) of the Court of Justice of the European Union.
They also run counter to the Commission’s 2022 guidance on taxis and PHVs. The Commission has already been examining Spanish taxi/PHV rules through an EU pilot procedure. Against this background: 1.
Why were the Catalan bill’s broader restrictions on PHVs left out of the Commission’s assessment under the TRIS procedure?
How will the Commission ensure compliance with Article 49 TFEU and the Prestige and Limousine judgment, taking account of its 2022 guidance on taxis and PHVs?
What is the status of the EU pilot procedure on Spanish taxi/PHV rules, and will the Commission pursue infringement proceedings under Article 258 TFEU if breaches persist?
